adult.prompt: Using ONLY this real Common Kestrel photo as the anatomical reference, create one new photoreal adult male Common Kestrel flying left. This replaces a failed artificial-looking website asset. Preserve the organic living-bird quality of this photograph, not an illustration or 3D model. Reorient to the left: wings diagonal lower-left to upper-right, camera from below and somewhat to the side so the side of the gray head, dark natural-size eye and tiny hooked beak are clearly seen in left profile. Head-to-tail axis nearly horizontal, tail extends to right slightly downward. Slim compact kestrel body, naturally integrated shoulder wing joints, tapered pointed falcon wings and long gray tail slightly spread with black terminal band. Tucked feet almost hidden. Gray male head, pale buff spotted underside, neutral pale gray-brown barred underwings; do not paint rufous back coloration onto the underwings. Real photographic fine feathers with irregular soft texture, no embossed feather plates, no swollen pigeon chest, no oversized toy eye, no eagle body or fingered eagle wings. Square canvas, whole bird completely visible, comfortably centered with 9 percent margin around extreme feathers. Solid saturated blue background #0055FF for clean local cutout, no blue light spill, no checkerboard or text. Species anatomy must come from the photograph. The output should look like a sharply focused real wildlife photograph with neutral diffuse daylight.
